analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: changelog.d/nemotron-super-production.md (head lines 149-157) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph near head lines 456-468). No source, config, endpoint, key-handling, attestation or authorization code is in the supplied diff, so no trust boundary, cryptographic, authorization or billing behavior changes in this PR itself.

The docs describe performance changes that live in code outside this batch: NAX-GPU NVFP4 expert kernels (ModelOptNVFP4NAXExperts), NAX dense linear decode (ModelOptNAXDenseLinear), a chunked NAX Mamba scan, windowed verify-window submission (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_WINDOW_SUBMIT) and fused decode kernels (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_FUSION). The docs claim decode tokens are unchanged and that accuracy stays within the teacher-forced gate (top-1 78.09% vs 78.12%).

These kernel claims fall under T-007 (output integrity) and TB-007 (inference engine). I could not verify them from the supplied evidence. Two points need review in the actual code PR:
- New env knobs and kernels must not alter the memory accounting, activation or prefill-lane reservations, or the prefix-cache checkpoint exactness that T-041 relies on.
- The new kernels run on KV and prefix-cache state, but the docs say the expert summation order differs, so a prefix checkpoint restore may no longer reproduce a cold prefill bit for bit. The docs at base lines 229-231 claim exactness, so the exactness claim may now be stale. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a demonstrated vulnerability.

No prompt data, key, attestation or cache-scoping behavior is described as changed. No findings. I recommend that reviewers of the accompanying code verify the memory-ledger and prefix-exactness claims.
